statement: Main experimental confounder: because successive amended clauses retain much of the original wording, an end-task answer-accuracy metric can be insensitive to version confusion - retrieving the superseded version may yield the same answer string and score as retrieving the in-force version. A temporal relevance term could therefore appear to help (or fail to help) for reasons unrelated to selecting the correct revision; the effect can only be attributed to temporal ranking if temporal-contamination/leakage is measured separately and query labels are not correlated with recency. Additionally, if the correct passage happens to be the most recent version in most queries, a pure recency prior wins without any validity reasoning.

evidence.quote: reducing temporal evidence leakage from 10.8% to 1.7%
even when provided with an updated evidence corpus (a roughly 15 point drop in accuracy)
